question:
As of 2026, consider the following statements regarding the RBI's draft directions on the Term Money Market:

1. All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs) and eligible NBFCs/HFCs will be permitted to participate as both borrowers and lenders.

2. Companies will be allowed to participate only as lenders.

3. The borrowing limit for NBFCs and HFCs has been capped at 200% of their Net Owned Funds (NOF).

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released draft directions to broaden participation in the Term Money Market by allowing All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs), eligible Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), and companies to participate.

The draft directions aim to deepen liquidity, strengthen the short-term funding market, and improve the efficiency of India's money market.

Under the proposed framework, AIFIs and eligible NBFCs/HFCs will be permitted to participate as both borrowers and lenders in the Term Money Market.

Detailed Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released draft directions to broaden participation in the Term Money Market by allowing All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs), eligible Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), and companies to participate.

The draft directions aim to deepen liquidity, strengthen the short-term funding market, and improve the efficiency of India's money market.

Under the proposed framework, AIFIs and eligible NBFCs/HFCs will be permitted to participate as both borrowers and lenders in the Term Money Market.

Companies will be allowed to participate only as lenders, thereby expanding the availability of funds in the short-term money market.

The RBI has proposed wider (Bharat-wide) participation to improve monetary policy transmission and strengthen the linkage between the overnight money market and longer-term interest rates.

The borrowing limit for NBFCs and HFCs has been capped at 200% of their Net Owned Funds (NOF).

Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) will be permitted to borrow up to 400% of their Net Owned Funds (NOF) through Term Money and Inter-Corporate Deposits (ICDs).

question: As of 2026, under the RBI's draft framework for secondary market transactions in Government Securities (G- Secs), what is the proposed minimum transaction size for retail investors?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued draft directions to simplify and consolidate regulations governing secondary market transactions in Government Securities (G-Secs), including 'When Issued'

(WI) trading, short selling, and Government Securities Lending (GSL) under a single regulatory framework.

To promote retail investor participation, RBI has proposed allowing individual investors to buy and sell Government Securities through their demat accounts using the NDS-OM (Negotiated Dealing System–Order Matching) platform or the Stock Broker Connect facility.

The minimum transaction size for retail investors under the proposed framework will be ₹10,000.

Detailed Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued draft directions to simplify and consolidate regulations governing secondary market transactions in Government Securities (G-Secs), including 'When Issued'

(WI) trading, short selling, and Government Securities Lending (GSL) under a single regulatory framework.

The draft framework aims to enhance transparency, improve market liquidity, strengthen price discovery, and increase retail participation in the Government Securities (G-Secs) market.

To promote retail investor participation, RBI has proposed allowing individual investors to buy and sell Government Securities through their demat accounts using the NDS-OM (Negotiated Dealing System–Order Matching) platform or the Stock Broker Connect facility.

The minimum transaction size for retail investors under the proposed framework will be ₹10,000.

The draft directions integrate the Government Securities Lending (GSL) Framework, allowing eligible participants to borrow Government Securities to meet delivery obligations arising from short sale transactions, thereby improving market liquidity.

The framework continues to permit 'When Issued' (WI) trading, enabling eligible participants to trade Government Securities after their announcement but before their actual issuance, thereby facilitating efficient price discovery.

Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) and Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) are permitted to take both long and short positions up to 25% of the notified auction amount in a specific Government Security.

Other eligible participants are allowed to hold only long positions up to 10% of the notified auction amount in a specific Government Security.

question: In 2026, the SC120 Semi-Cryogenic Stage being developed by ISRO is intended to replace which existing stage of the Launch Vehicle Mark-III (LVM3)?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted a hot test of the Semi-Cryogenic Engine Power Head Test Article (PHTA) at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPC), Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu.

The hot test achieved 88% of the target thrust, generating 175 tonnes of thrust, marking a major milestone in the development of India's next-generation rocket propulsion system.

The test was the 8th hot test in the PHTA test series, following earlier successful tests at 47% (94 tonnes) and 60% (120 tonnes) of full thrust.

The successful 175-tonne test has provided ISRO with confidence to proceed towards the full-thrust demonstration of 200 tonnes.

The SC120 propulsion stage is being developed to replace the existing L110 core stage of the Launch Vehicle Mark-III (LVM3) rocket.

Detailed Explanation:

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted a hot test of the Semi-Cryogenic Engine Power Head Test Article (PHTA) at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPC), Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu.

The hot test achieved 88% of the target thrust, generating 175 tonnes of thrust, marking a major milestone in the development of India's next-generation rocket propulsion system.

The test was the 8th hot test in the PHTA test series, following earlier successful tests at 47% (94 tonnes) and 60% (120 tonnes) of full thrust.

The successful 175-tonne test has provided ISRO with confidence to proceed towards the full-thrust demonstration of 200 tonnes.

The SE2000 Semi-Cryogenic Engine is designed to produce 2,000 kilonewtons (kN) of thrust and will power the SC120 (Semi- Cryogenic Stage).

The SC120 propulsion stage is being developed to replace the existing L110 core stage of the Launch Vehicle Mark-III (LVM3) rocket.

The upgraded SC120 stage is expected to increase the Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO) payload capacity of LVM3 from 4 tonnes to 5 tonnes.

The Low Earth Orbit (LEO) payload capacity of LVM3 is also expected to increase from 8 tonnes to 10 tonnes after the induction of the SC120 stage.

The SE2000 engine uses Liquid Oxygen (LOX) as the oxidiser and Kerosene as the fuel, operating on an Oxidiser-Rich Staged Combustion Cycle.

The observance recognises the role of GST in improving tax compliance, enhancing transparency, and strengthening India's economic integration.

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) under the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) successfully conducted India’s first Satellite-Based Landing System (SLS) approach on a commercial jet aircraft using an IndiGo Airbus A320 at Maharana Pratap Airport, Udaipur, Rajasthan.

The demonstration used GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation), India’s indigenous Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS), marking a major milestone in satellite-guided precision landings in India.

The approach was carried out using Localiser Performance with Vertical Guidance (LPV) technology, which provides both lateral (left- right) and vertical (up-down) guidance to the runway.

LPV offers landing precision comparable to an Instrument Landing System (ILS) but does not require specialised ground-based equipment to be installed at the airport.

Short Explanation:

International Plastic Bag Free Day is observed every year on 3 July to encourage people to reduce the use of single-use plastic bags and help eliminate plastic pollution.

In 2015, the European Union adopted directives to reduce the consumption of single- use plastic bags.

Bangladesh became the first country to ban thin single-use plastic bags.

Detailed Explanation:

International Plastic Bag Free Day is observed every year on 3 July to encourage people to reduce the use of single-use plastic bags and help eliminate plastic pollution.

The day spreads awareness that a plastic bag- free world is possible by promoting sustainable and environmentally friendly alternatives.

The initiative was established by the Bag Free World organisation, which launched campaigns promoting a plastic-free world.

The first International Plastic Bag Free Day was observed on 3 July 2008, initiated by Rezero, a member of Zero Waste Europe.

In 2015, the European Union adopted directives to reduce the consumption of single- use plastic bags.

Bangladesh became the first country to ban thin single-use plastic bags.

question: In July 2026, which bank partnered with NPCI and JP Morgan Payments to provide real-time Foreign Exchange (FX) rates for cross-border UPI transactions?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) partnered with HSBC India and JP Morgan Payments to enable real-time Foreign Exchange (FX) settlement for cross-border Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions.

The initiative aims to improve the international payment experience by providing greater transparency, faster settlement, and real-time currency conversion for Indian users.

Under the partnership, HSBC India will serve as the banking partner, providing real-time Foreign Exchange (FX) rates through direct Application Programming Interface (API) integration.

HSBC India's global banking network will support secure, 24×7 cross-border transactions, making overseas UPI payments faster and more efficient.

JP Morgan Payments will facilitate real-time FX conversion and multi-currency settlement, enhancing the efficiency of international digital payments.

Detailed Explanation:

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) partnered with HSBC India and JP Morgan Payments to enable real-time Foreign Exchange (FX) settlement for cross-border Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions.

The initiative aims to improve the international payment experience by providing greater transparency, faster settlement, and real-time currency conversion for Indian users.

Under the partnership, HSBC India will serve as the banking partner, providing real-time Foreign Exchange (FX) rates through direct Application Programming Interface (API) integration.

HSBC India's global banking network will support secure, 24×7 cross-border transactions, making overseas UPI payments faster and more efficient.

JP Morgan Payments will facilitate real-time FX conversion and multi-currency settlement, enhancing the efficiency of international digital payments.

The collaboration combines UPI's expanding global acceptance with JP Morgan's foreign exchange expertise to simplify international payment settlements.

Indian users making payments abroad will be able to view the exact payment amount in Indian Rupees (INR) before confirming the transaction.

Overseas merchants will continue to receive payments in their local currencies, while Indian customers pay directly from their Indian bank accounts.

The initiative eliminates the need to rely solely on cash or international credit/debit cards for payments abroad.

UPI is currently accepted in 9 countries:

Singapore, United Arab Emirates (UAE), Nepal, Bhutan, Mauritius, France, Sri Lanka, Qatar, and Cambodia.

NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) recently partnered with ACLEDA Bank Plc to launch UPI acceptance in Cambodia.

UPI is further expanding its international presence to countries such as Japan, Maldives, and Greece through NPCI International (NIPL).

question: Under the newly notified Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme, 2026, what minimum balance must an EPFO member retain in the EPF account before making a partial withdrawal?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Central Government has notified the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme, 2026, introducing significant changes to the partial withdrawal rules for members of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

The revised scheme came into effect on 29 June 2026.

The scheme introduces a minimum balance requirement, expands the list of eligible purposes for partial withdrawals, and supports the Government's digital transformation initiatives.

Under the new rules, EPFO members must retain at least 25% of the balance in their Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) account before making any partial withdrawal.

Detailed Explanation:

The Central Government has notified the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme, 2026, introducing significant changes to the partial withdrawal rules for members of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).

The revised scheme came into effect on 29 June 2026.

The scheme introduces a minimum balance requirement, expands the list of eligible purposes for partial withdrawals, and supports the Government's digital transformation initiatives.

Under the new rules, EPFO members must retain at least 25% of the balance in their Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) account before making any partial withdrawal.

The minimum balance requirement applies to both employee contributions and employer contributions.

For example, if the eligible EPF balance is ₹1 lakh, the member must retain ₹25,000, while up to ₹75,000 can be withdrawn, subject to the prescribed conditions.

question: Under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which came into force from 1 July 2026, the statutory wage employment guarantee for every eligible rural household has been increased to how many days?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan launched the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB-G RAM (G)] from Mukkavaripalli village, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.

The mission is being implemented under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which came into force from 1 July 2026.

The Act increases the statutory wage employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days per financial year for every eligible rural household.

Detailed Explanation:

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan launched the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB-G RAM (G)] from Mukkavaripalli village, Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.

The launch event was attended by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan.

The mission is being implemented under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which came into force from 1 July 2026.

The Act increases the statutory wage employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days per financial year for every eligible rural household.

Employment will be provided to adults willing to undertake unskilled manual work, and workers will continue to receive unemployment allowance if employment is not provided within the prescribed time.

The scheme replaces the earlier framework of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with an expanded rural employment and livelihood programme.

question: From 2027, the International Booker Prize will be officially renamed as the_________
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The International Booker Prize will be officially renamed the Bukhman International Booker Prize from 2027 following a 10-year funding agreement (2027–2036) with Bukhman Philanthropies.

The annual prize money will increase from £50,000 to £100,000, making it one of the world's richest international literary awards.

Detailed Explanation:

The International Booker Prize will be officially renamed the Bukhman International Booker Prize from 2027 following a 10-year funding agreement (2027–2036) with Bukhman Philanthropies.

The annual prize money will increase from £50,000 to £100,000, making it one of the world's richest international literary awards.

The prize money will continue to be shared equally between the author and the translator, recognising the important contribution of translators.

Bukhman Philanthropies was founded by Daria Bukhman and Dmitri Bukhman.

question: As per the news, the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) on 3 July 2026 accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to multiple defence acquisition proposals worth approximately__________
explanation:

The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to multiple defence acquisition proposals on 3 July 2026.

The total value of the AoN approvals is approximately ₹52,000 crore.

Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) is the in- principle administrative approval required before the procurement of defence equipment.

For the Indian Army, DAC approved the procurement of AKASH TARANG Anti- Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) Electronic Warfare System, Man Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MPATGM) Systems, Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM) Weapon System, Very Short Range Air Defence System (V-SHORADS), Active Protection System (APS) for Tanks, and Jet- Based Kamikaze Drone System.

Detailed Explanation:

The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), chaired by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh, accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) to multiple defence acquisition proposals on 3 July 2026.

The total value of the AoN approvals is approximately ₹52,000 crore.

Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) is the in- principle administrative approval required before the procurement of defence equipment.

For the Indian Army, DAC approved the procurement of AKASH TARANG Anti- Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) Electronic Warfare System, Man Portable Anti-Tank Guided Missile (MPATGM) Systems, Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM) Weapon System, Very Short Range Air Defence System (V-SHORADS), Active Protection System (APS) for Tanks, and Jet- Based Kamikaze Drone System.

The procedure has been developed in accordance with DGCA regulations and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs).

Point-in-Space (PinS) is a satellite-guided instrument approach procedure designed specifically for helicopter operations.

The system is based on Performance-Based Navigation (PBN) using the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) together with India’s GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation) system.

The PinS procedure enables helicopters to perform safe and precise approaches to heliports without depending on ground-based radar or Instrument Landing System (ILS) infrastructure.

question: As per the news, which type of tax system is Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Goods and Services Tax (GST) was launched on 1 July 2017 under the vision of "One Nation, One Tax", replacing 17 indirect taxes and 13 cesses with a unified indirect tax system.

GST eliminated the cascading effect of taxes (tax on tax), created a common national market, and strengthened the vision of "Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat."

GST is a destination-based consumption tax, where tax revenue accrues to the State in which goods or services are finally consumed.

GST is levied on the supply of goods and services rather than separately on manufacture, sale, or services.

Detailed Explanation:

Goods and Services Tax (GST) was launched on 1 July 2017 under the vision of "One Nation, One Tax", replacing 17 indirect taxes and 13 cesses with a unified indirect tax system.

GST eliminated the cascading effect of taxes (tax on tax), created a common national market, and strengthened the vision of "Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat."

GST is a destination-based consumption tax, where tax revenue accrues to the State in which goods or services are finally consumed.

GST is levied on the supply of goods and services rather than separately on manufacture, sale, or services.

India follows a Dual GST Model, comprising Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST), State Goods and Services Tax (SGST), and Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) for inter-state supplies.

IGST is levied on inter-state supplies, and its rate is generally twice the CGST/SGST rate.

The GST Council is a statutory body that promotes co-operative federalism by enabling joint decision-making between the Central Government and State Governments.

The study detected compact radio emission from the centres of nearly one- quarter of the galaxies, confirming the presence of weakly accreting supermassive black holes.

Detailed Explanation:

Astronomers discovered a hidden population of weakly active supermassive black holes in nearby galaxies using high-resolution radio observations, revealing black holes that were previously difficult to detect.

The discovery is significant because weakly active black holes inject energy into their surroundings through jets and outflows, influencing star formation and the long-term evolution of galaxies.

Astronomers believe that almost every galaxy contains a supermassive black hole at its centre, but many remain extremely faint and escape conventional detection.

The research was conducted by an international team of astronomers, including Dr. Aru Beri from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

The team used the e-MERLIN radio array to observe 280 nearby galaxies selected from the Palomar sample, examining their central regions on parsec scales.

The study detected compact radio emission from the centres of nearly one- quarter of the galaxies, confirming the presence of weakly accreting supermassive black holes.

question: Recently in news, the first static ground test of ISRO’s Sub-Orbital Launch Vehicle for Experiments (SOLVE) was conducted at which centre?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the first static ground test of the Sub-Orbital Launch Vehicle for Experiments (SOLVE).

The test was conducted at the Static Test Facility of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.

SOLVE is a solid-propellant, sub-orbital launch vehicle developed as a dedicated test platform for the Gaganyaan Mission.

The test successfully validated the solid motor for the Integrated Parachute Test (IPT) of the Gaganyaan Crew Module.

Detailed Explanation:

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the first static ground test of the Sub-Orbital Launch Vehicle for Experiments (SOLVE).

The test was conducted at the Static Test Facility of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.

SOLVE is a solid-propellant, sub-orbital launch vehicle developed as a dedicated test platform for the Gaganyaan Mission.

The test successfully validated the solid motor for the Integrated Parachute Test (IPT) of the Gaganyaan Crew Module.

SOLVE is designed to simulate the Crew Module's deceleration at an altitude of 10 km to 17 km before human spaceflight.

The primary objective of SOLVE is to test the Crew Module’s deceleration system, parachute deployment, and safe recovery under realistic mission conditions.

During SOLVE missions, the Crew Module will separate from the launch vehicle at an altitude of 10–17 km and deploy a sequence of 10 parachutes before sea splashdown.

question: As per the recent development, POWERGRID secured a Japanese Yen 80 billion Green Loan to finance which of the following transmission projects?

explanation:

The JPY 80 billion Green Loan is among India's largest green financing arrangements for the power transmission sector and supports the integration of Renewable Energy (RE) into the national power grid.

The loan agreement was signed in June 2026 to finance the Khavda–Nagpur High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Transmission Project.

Detailed Explanation:

Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID), a 'Maharatna' Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) under the Ministry of Power (MoP), secured a Japanese Yen (JPY) 80 billion Green Loan from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC).

The JPY 80 billion Green Loan is among India's largest green financing arrangements for the power transmission sector and supports the integration of Renewable Energy (RE) into the national power grid.

The loan agreement was signed in June 2026 to finance the Khavda–Nagpur High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Transmission Project.

Detailed Explanation:

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has launched a crackdown on "Dark Patterns" in digital insurance platforms to curb mis-selling, improve transparency, strengthen consumer protection, and enhance public trust in the insurance sector.

Dark Patterns are deceptive design techniques used on websites and mobile applications that manipulate users into sharing personal information, accepting unwanted products, paying hidden charges, facing difficult policy cancellations, or receiving unsolicited calls and messages.

Common examples of Dark Patterns include forcing users to share personal details before viewing insurance products, making policy cancellation difficult, spam calls, hidden charges, and misleading website/app interfaces.

Recently in news, consider the following statements regarding POSHAN Abhiyaan and Poshan Tracker:

2. Poshan Tracker was launched in March 2021 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in collaboration with the National e- Governance Division.

3. Poshan Tracker replaced the manual registers maintained by Anganwadi Workers with smartphone-based digital reporting.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

POSHAN Abhiyaan (Prime Minister’s Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment) is India’s flagship National Nutrition Mission, launched on 8 March 2018, to improve nutrition outcomes through convergence, technology, and community mobilisation.

POSHAN Abhiyaan functions under the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) and follows a Jan Andolan (People’s Movement) approach with time-bound targets, digital monitoring, and a multi-ministerial framework.

Under Union Budget 2021–22, POSHAN Abhiyaan, Anganwadi Services, and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls were merged under Mission POSHAN 2.0 (Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0).

Poshan Tracker is a mobile-based governance application and the digital backbone of POSHAN Abhiyaan, launched in March 2021 by the MoWCD in collaboration with the National e- Governance Division (NeGD).

Detailed Explanation:

POSHAN Abhiyaan (Prime Minister’s Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment) is India’s flagship National Nutrition Mission, launched on 8 March 2018, to improve nutrition outcomes through convergence, technology, and community mobilisation.

POSHAN Abhiyaan functions under the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) and follows a Jan Andolan (People’s Movement) approach with time-bound targets, digital monitoring, and a multi-ministerial framework.

Under Union Budget 2021–22, POSHAN Abhiyaan, Anganwadi Services, and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls were merged under Mission POSHAN 2.0 (Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0).

Poshan Tracker is a mobile-based governance application and the digital backbone of POSHAN Abhiyaan, launched in March 2021 by the MoWCD in collaboration with the National e- Governance Division (NeGD).

Poshan Tracker enables near real-time monitoring of nutrition, Anganwadi infrastructure, service delivery, beneficiary coverage, and growth monitoring through a unified digital platform.

The application supports dynamic identification of stunting, wasting, underweight, Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), and overweight/obesity among children using WHO Child Growth Standards.

Before Poshan Tracker, Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) maintained 11 manual registers; the platform has replaced these with smartphone- based digital reporting, reducing delays and improving service delivery.

question: Recently in news, scientists identified the world’s oldest accurately dated banyan tree in which district of Bihar?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Scientists identified a banyan tree in Munger district, Bihar, as the world's oldest accurately dated banyan tree, estimating its age at around 700 years using high-precision radiocarbon dating.

The research was published in the journal Quaternary Research and is the first scientific study to determine the age of a banyan tree (Ficus benghalensis) using scientific evidence instead of folklore, historical records, or local traditions.

The study was led by Dr. Trina Bose of the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), Lucknow, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), along with Dr. Mayank Shekhar and Dr. Akhilesh K. Yadava.

Detailed Explanation:

Scientists identified a banyan tree in Munger district, Bihar, as the world's oldest accurately dated banyan tree, estimating its age at around 700 years using high-precision radiocarbon dating.

The research was published in the journal Quaternary Research and is the first scientific study to determine the age of a banyan tree (Ficus benghalensis) using scientific evidence instead of folklore, historical records, or local traditions.

The study was led by Dr. Trina Bose of the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), Lucknow, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), along with Dr. Mayank Shekhar and Dr. Akhilesh K. Yadava.

The study was initiated after the Bihar Forest Department requested the scientific determination of the age of the Munger Banyan Tree.

The researchers developed a new scientific methodology because tropical broadleaf trees generally lack distinct annual growth rings, making conventional dendrochronology unsuitable.

question: Recently in news, the Jawahar Institute of Mountaineering & Winter Sports (JIM & WS), Pahalgam conducted a mountaineering expedition to which massif in Ladakh?

question: Recently in news, which company unveiled the world’s first sub-1 nanometre (0.7 nm / 7 angstrom) semiconductor chip technology?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

IBM unveiled the world's first sub-1 nanometre (0.7 nm / 7 angstrom) semiconductor chip technology, marking a major breakthrough in next-generation computing and semiconductor manufacturing.

The innovation moves chip manufacturing beyond the traditional nanometre era toward atomic-scale (angstrom-level) engineering, overcoming the physical limits of conventional chip scaling.

Detailed Explanation:

IBM unveiled the world's first sub-1 nanometre (0.7 nm / 7 angstrom) semiconductor chip technology, marking a major breakthrough in next-generation computing and semiconductor manufacturing.

The innovation moves chip manufacturing beyond the traditional nanometre era toward atomic-scale (angstrom-level) engineering, overcoming the physical limits of conventional chip scaling.

The chip is built using IBM's 3D "Nanostack"

transistor architecture, the industry's first three-dimensional nanosheet-based transistor design.

The 0.7 nm (7 angstrom) chip packs nearly 100 billion transistors on a chip approximately the size of a fingernail, almost twice the transistor density of IBM's 2 nm chip launched in 2021.

According to IBM, the new chip is expected to deliver up to 50% higher performance or 70% greater energy efficiency compared to its 2 nm node technology.

Detailed Explanation:

The Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) was launched in 2014– 15 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) to promote farm mechanization across India.

Objective: To "reach the unreached" by extending mechanization benefits to small & marginal farmers, women farmers, SCs, STs, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Self- Help Groups (SHGs), and rural entrepreneurs.

Farm mechanization covers the entire crop cycle including land preparation, sowing, irrigation, plant protection, harvesting, and post- harvest management, improving productivity and reducing labour dependence.

Special emphasis has been given to North- Eastern (NE) States and underserved regions to reduce regional disparities in mechanization.

Since inception, ₹9,404.47 crore has been provided under SMAM, supporting the distribution of 21.61 lakh agricultural machines to individual farmers.

Under SMAM, 27,554 Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), 646 Hi-Tech Hubs, and 25,608 Farm Machinery Banks (FMBs) have been established.

question: Recently, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the Reserve Bank– Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS), 2026, replacing which of the following schemes?

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the Reserve Bank–Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS), 2026, replacing the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021, with effect from 1 July 2026.

RB-IOS, 2026 aims to provide a faster, simpler, free, and non-adversarial mechanism for resolving customer complaints against RBI- regulated financial entities.

Complaints, appeals, and awards filed under the 2021 Scheme will continue to be governed by the earlier provisions.

Detailed Explanation:

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the Reserve Bank–Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS), 2026, replacing the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021, with effect from 1 July 2026.

RB-IOS, 2026 aims to provide a faster, simpler, free, and non-adversarial mechanism for resolving customer complaints against RBI- regulated financial entities.

Complaints, appeals, and awards filed under the 2021 Scheme will continue to be governed by the earlier provisions.

The scheme follows the "One Nation, One Ombudsman" approach, allowing customers to file complaints without considering the geographical location of the customer or the regulated entity.

RB-IOS, 2026 covers Banks, Eligible NBFCs, Non-Bank Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI) Issuers, and Credit Information Companies (CICs) regulated by RBI.

Complaints against RBI-regulated entities not covered under the scheme are handled through Consumer Education and Protection Cells (CEPCs) and other RBI grievance redress mechanisms.

question: Recently, ISRO successfully conducted the Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Test- 05 (IMAT-05) for which mission?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Test-05 (IMAT-05) for the Gaganyaan G1 Mission at the Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE) Drop Zone, Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh.

IMAT-05 was conducted to validate the Main Parachute System under maximum expected load conditions for the first uncrewed Gaganyaan G1 Mission.

During the test, a simulated payload was dropped from an altitude of 2.5 kilometres (km) using an Indian Air Force (IAF) IL-76 aircraft to verify the performance, reliability, and structural integrity of the Main Parachute System.

Detailed Explanation:

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully conducted the Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Test-05 (IMAT-05) for the Gaganyaan G1 Mission at the Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE) Drop Zone, Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh.

IMAT-05 was conducted to validate the Main Parachute System under maximum expected load conditions for the first uncrewed Gaganyaan G1 Mission.

During the test, a simulated payload was dropped from an altitude of 2.5 kilometres (km) using an Indian Air Force (IAF) IL-76 aircraft to verify the performance, reliability, and structural integrity of the Main Parachute System.

IMAT-05 is the 5th test in the series of Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Tests (IMAT) conducted to qualify the Main Parachute for the Gaganyaan Mission.

The descent sequence successfully deployed the Extractor Parachute, Drogue Parachute, and Main Parachute, with the Main Parachute reducing the payload to a safe terminal velocity before landing.

The Gaganyaan Crew Module Deceleration System consists of 10 parachutes of 4 different types: 2 Apex Cover Separation Parachutes, 2 Drogue Parachutes, 3 Pilot Parachutes, and 3 Main Parachutes.

question: As per the news, how much loan has the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) committed as part of the World Bank’s $890 million financing package for India's PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?

question: As per the news, who launched the new Letter of Authorisation (LoA) regime to promote sustainable high-seas fishing and strengthen India's Blue Economy?

Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan launched the new Letter of Authorisation (LoA) regime to promote sustainable high-seas fishing, enhance the income of fishing communities, and strengthen India's Blue Economy.

The Letter of Authorisation (LoA) is a regulatory mechanism that authorises Indian fishing vessels to undertake fishing operations in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and the high seas through a simplified and transparent approval process.

The initiative aims to promote sustainable deep-sea fishing, increase access to high- value marine species, reduce pressure on overexploited coastal fisheries, and improve the utilisation of marine resources.

India has a coastline of over 11,000 kilometres and an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of nearly 2.4 million square kilometres (24 lakh sq. km.), but most fishing activities are currently confined within 40–50 nautical miles from the coast.

The new regime is expected to strengthen Fish Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs) and fishing cooperatives, generate employment opportunities, increase seafood exports, and expand India's presence in the global seafood market.

Scientists at the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research–Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CSIR-CIMFR), Dhanbad, Jharkhand, developed India’s first mobile “Liquid Tree”, called the Smart Algal Liquid Tree (SALT).

SALT (Smart Algal Liquid Tree) is an innovative air purification system designed to improve air quality in densely populated urban and industrial areas where planting conventional trees is difficult.

SALT is a compact container filled with water and microalgae, which are microscopic single- celled organisms that perform photosynthesis by absorbing carbon dioxide (CO₂) and releasing oxygen (O₂).

Microalgae are responsible for generating nearly 50% of the Earth’s oxygen through photosynthesis.

SALT works by drawing or bubbling polluted air through the algae-filled tank, where CO₂ is absorbed, oxygen is released, and certain air pollutants are trapped or biologically processed.

question: Recently, the Ministry of MSME mandated all operating Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME invoices through which RBI-authorised digital platform?

The new mandate implements a key announcement of the Union Budget FY2026– 27, aimed at strengthening MSME financing and ensuring timely payments.

Detailed Explanation:

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), through a notification issued on 30 June 2026, mandated all operating Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME invoices for goods and services through Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platforms authorised by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

The new mandate implements a key announcement of the Union Budget FY2026– 27, aimed at strengthening MSME financing and ensuring timely payments.

Under the new framework, CPSEs must route and settle MSME invoices through TReDS, enhancing transparency, accountability, and payment discipline.

CPSEs are required to disclose details of MSME invoices processed through TReDS and obtain a Statutory Auditor’s Certificate confirming TReDS registration and compliance during the annual audit.

The initiative will facilitate collateral-free working capital for MSMEs by enabling invoice discounting before the payment due date, improving their liquidity.

The reform is expected to make CPSEs role models for timely payment practices among large corporate buyers.

Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) is an RBI-authorised digital platform, operational since 2017, designed to facilitate financing and discounting of trade receivables of MSMEs due from corporate buyers, Government Departments, and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) through competitive bidding by multiple financiers.

question: Recently, which country successfully achieved the first controlled recovery of an orbital-class reusable rocket booster following the maiden launch of the Long March-10B carrier rocket?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

China successfully achieved the first controlled recovery of an orbital-class reusable rocket booster following the maiden launch of the Long March-10B carrier rocket from Hainan Province, China.

The Long March-10B was developed by the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology (CALT) and successfully placed its payload into orbit, while its first-stage booster was recovered on a sea-based net platform.

Detailed Explanation:

China successfully achieved the first controlled recovery of an orbital-class reusable rocket booster following the maiden launch of the Long March-10B carrier rocket from Hainan Province, China.

The Long March-10B was developed by the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology (CALT) and successfully placed its payload into orbit, while its first-stage booster was recovered on a sea-based net platform.

This mission marks China’s first-ever controlled recovery of an orbital-class reusable rocket booster, representing a major breakthrough in the country’s reusable space technology.

The achievement comes more than a decade after SpaceX, which became the first company in the world to recover an orbital-class rocket booster with the Falcon 9 in 2015.

The Long March-10B is a liquid-fuelled reusable launch vehicle designed to support China’s reusable rocket programme and reduce launch costs through booster reuse.

The rocket is 63 metres tall, has a 5-metre diameter, a lift-off mass of 760 tonnes, generates 890 tonnes of thrust, and can carry a 16-tonne payload to Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

question:
As per the news, consider the following statements regarding the World Bank Country Income Classification (FY2027):

1. India continues to be classified as a Lower-Middle-Income Economy.

2. India's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita under the Atlas Method was USD 2,760 in 2025.

3. Delhi ranks first among Indian states with a GNI per capita of USD 6,217 and has crossed the World Bank's Upper- Middle-Income threshold.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

According to the World Bank Country Income Classification (FY2027), India continues to be classified as a Lower-Middle-Income Economy.

India's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita under the Atlas Method was USD 2,760 (2025), and the country has remained in the Lower-Middle-Income category since 2009.

Delhi ranks first among Indian states with a GNI per capita of USD 6,217, followed by Karnataka (USD 5,579), Telangana (USD 5,407), Tamil Nadu (USD 5,329), and Gujarat (USD 4,734).

Maharashtra (USD 4,628), Haryana (USD 4,627), and Kerala (USD 4,610) narrowly missed the Upper-Middle-Income threshold by USD 8, USD 9, and USD 26, respectively.

Detailed Explanation:

According to the World Bank Country Income Classification (FY2027), India continues to be classified as a Lower-Middle-Income Economy.

India's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita under the Atlas Method was USD 2,760 (2025), and the country has remained in the Lower-Middle-Income category since 2009.

The World Bank classifies economies annually on 1 July based on the previous year's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita calculated using the Atlas Method.

Under the FY2027 World Bank Income Classification, Low Income economies have GNI per capita of USD 1,175 or less, Lower- Middle Income economies have USD 1,176– 4,635, Upper-Middle Income economies have USD 4,636–14,375, and High Income economies have above USD 14,375.

Five Indian states have crossed the World Bank's Upper-Middle-Income threshold (GNI per capita above USD 4,636).

Delhi ranks first among Indian states with a GNI per capita of USD 6,217, followed by Karnataka (USD 5,579), Telangana (USD 5,407), Tamil Nadu (USD 5,329), and Gujarat (USD 4,734).

Maharashtra (USD 4,628), Haryana (USD 4,627), and Kerala (USD 4,610) narrowly missed the Upper-Middle-Income threshold by USD 8, USD 9, and USD 26, respectively.

The defence package also includes the export of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles and cooperation in defence technology, maritime security, and critical minerals.

question: As per the news, the advanced ammonia sensing platform was developed by researchers from which institute?

explanation:
Short Explanation:

Scientists have developed an advanced ammonia sensing platform capable of detecting ammonia gas at extremely low concentrations while operating efficiently at room temperature.

The technology was developed by researchers at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

The sensor is based on a hybrid Vanadium Oxide–Vanadium Sulfide (VOx/VS2) heterostructure, engineered through a controlled surface transformation process.

Detailed Explanation:

Scientists have developed an advanced ammonia sensing platform capable of detecting ammonia gas at extremely low concentrations while operating efficiently at room temperature.

The technology was developed by researchers at the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

The sensor is based on a hybrid Vanadium Oxide–Vanadium Sulfide (VOx/VS2) heterostructure, engineered through a controlled surface transformation process.

The VOx/VS2 heterostructure creates abundant active sites for ammonia adsorption and enhances charge transport, resulting in rapid, highly selective, and highly sensitive ammonia detection.

The sensor can detect ammonia concentrations as low as 319 parts per billion (ppb), which is well below occupational safety limits.

question: As per the RBI's draft amendment on acquisition of major shareholding in banks, after obtaining one-time RBI approval, eligible institutional investors can increase or retain their stake in the same banking company up to what limit without seeking fresh approval?

options.text: 5% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights
7.5% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights
10% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights
15% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights
26% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights

explanation:
Short Explanation:

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released a draft amendment proposing a one-time approval mechanism for eligible institutional investors to acquire and retain major shareholding (5% or more) in the same banking company without seeking repeated approvals.

Under the proposed framework, prior RBI approval will continue to be mandatory for the first acquisition of a major shareholding in a bank.

After obtaining the one-time approval, eligible investors can increase or retain their stake in the same bank up to 10% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights without seeking fresh RBI approval every time their holding falls below and later exceeds 5%.

Detailed Explanation:

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released a draft amendment proposing a one-time approval mechanism for eligible institutional investors to acquire and retain major shareholding (5% or more) in the same banking company without seeking repeated approvals.

Under the proposed framework, prior RBI approval will continue to be mandatory for the first acquisition of a major shareholding in a bank.

After obtaining the one-time approval, eligible investors can increase or retain their stake in the same bank up to 10% of the paid-up share capital or voting rights without seeking fresh RBI approval every time their holding falls below and later exceeds 5%.

The proposed facility will be available only to "Qualifying Persons", including SEBI- registered Mutual Funds, IRDAI-registered Insurance Companies, and PFRDA-registered Pension Funds.

To qualify, these institutional investors must not belong to the promoter group or group entities of the concerned banking company.

The proposal applies to Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Payments Banks, and Local Area Banks (LABs).

Under the existing framework, any investor whose holding falls below 5% must obtain fresh RBI approval before acquiring another major shareholding, even in the same bank.

Detailed Explanation:

question: Recently, since which financial year has the Services Sector continuously contributed more than 50% of India's Gross Value Added (GVA)?

The ISP measures short-term changes in the volume of output produced by the formal services sector relative to the base year, and should not be equated with Gross Value Added (GVA) used for GDP estimation.

The Index of Services Production (ISP) is designed as a high-frequency macroeconomic indicator to capture the short- term performance of the formal services sector, complementing the Index of Industrial Production (IIP).

The base year for the trial ISP is 2024–25, and the first index has been released for April 2026.

The trial ISP currently covers 19 sub-sectors, representing nearly 60% of India's formal services sector.

question: Recently, the Government of India revised the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) on petroleum product exports. By how much was the SAED on diesel exports increased?

Diesel (Exports): Increased from ₹8.5/litre to ₹15.5/litre Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) (Exports): Increased from ₹7.5/litre to ₹14.5/litre Petrol (Exports): Reduced from ₹4/litre to ₹2.5/litre

Detailed Explanation:

The Government of India has revised the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), commonly known as the windfall tax, on the export of petroleum products with effect from 16 July 2026.

The revised SAED rates are:

question: Recently, researchers from IACS and SNBNCBS developed a new porous organic anode material for high-performance lithium-ion batteries. What is the material called?
explanation:

Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), both under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), developed a new porous organic anode material for high- performance lithium-ion batteries.

The newly developed material is a Covalent Organic Framework (COF), a porous organic material designed to improve energy storage capacity, fast charging, and battery durability.

The research team was led by Dr. Urmimala Maitra (IACS) and Dr. Pradip Pachfule (SNBNCBS).

Detailed Explanation:

Researchers from the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS) and S. N.

Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), both under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), developed a new porous organic anode material for high- performance lithium-ion batteries.

The newly developed material is a Covalent Organic Framework (COF), a porous organic material designed to improve energy storage capacity, fast charging, and battery durability.

The research team was led by Dr. Urmimala Maitra (IACS) and Dr. Pradip Pachfule (SNBNCBS).

The COF-based anode material enables lithium ions to move more efficiently, resulting in faster charging, improved ion transport, enhanced charge storage, and greater structural stability.

Using the new COF material, the lithium-ion battery achieved 80% charging in just over one minute while maintaining excellent performance over repeated charging and discharging cycles.

question: Recently, which Kerala-based private spacetech startup successfully launched the satellite KOYO aboard SpaceX's Transporter- 17 mission?

The primary objective of the KOYO Mission is to qualify and validate space hardware before operational deployment through real-time in-orbit testing.

question: As per the RBI's final prudential norms, what is a Specified Non-Financial Asset (SNFA)?

options.text: A financial security acquired by banks for investment purposes
An immovable asset acquired by a lender in full or partial settlement of its claims against an NPA borrower
A movable asset pledged as collateral for a performing loan
A government-owned asset transferred to banks during recapitalisation
A digital asset acquired under insolvency proceedings

explanation:
Short Explanation:

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued final prudential norms for Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) regarding Specified Non- Financial Assets (SNFAs) acquired while resolving stressed loans or Non-Performing Assets (NPAs).

A Specified Non-Financial Asset (SNFA) is an immovable asset (such as property) acquired by a lender in full or partial settlement of its claims against a borrower, and can be acquired only when the lender's exposure is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA).

SNFAs may be acquired against full or partial extinguishment of a lender's exposure on a non-recourse basis.

Detailed Explanation:

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued final prudential norms for Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) regarding Specified Non- Financial Assets (SNFAs) acquired while resolving stressed loans or Non-Performing Assets (NPAs).

A Specified Non-Financial Asset (SNFA) is an immovable asset (such as property) acquired by a lender in full or partial settlement of its claims against a borrower, and can be acquired only when the lender's exposure is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA).

SNFAs may be acquired against full or partial extinguishment of a lender's exposure on a non-recourse basis.

If an SNFA is acquired through partial settlement of a loan, the remaining outstanding loan will be treated as a restructured loan and will be subject to the prudential norms applicable to restructured accounts.

Under the new framework, Banks, SFBs, and NBFCs cannot sell an SNFA back to the defaulting borrower or its related parties, and this restriction will continue even if the asset ceases to be classified as an SNFA.

All Banks, SFBs, and NBFCs must formulate Board-approved policies governing the acquisition, valuation, management, and disposal of SNFAs.

question: According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Financial Stability Report (FSR), which category of banks recorded the highest loan write-off ratio during FY2025–26?

Public Sector Banks (PSBs) held the largest share of bad loans, accounting for 63.2% of the total NPAs in the Indian banking system.

The Indian banking sector wrote off approximately ₹1.28 lakh crore of bad loans during FY2025–26, with an overall write-off ratio of 33.2%.

Foreign Banks recorded a write-off ratio of 39.6% during FY2025–26.

Private Sector Banks relied more on loan write-offs and provisioning buffers to improve their balance sheets due to higher defaults in unsecured retail loans, microfinance, personal loans, credit cards, and unsecured business loans.

Detailed Explanation:

According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Financial Stability Report (FSR), Private Sector Banks wrote off 49.7% of their Non- Performing Assets (NPAs) in FY2025–26, compared to 24.3% by Public Sector Banks (PSBs).

Public Sector Banks (PSBs) held the largest share of bad loans, accounting for 63.2% of the total NPAs in the Indian banking system.

The Indian banking sector wrote off approximately ₹1.28 lakh crore of bad loans during FY2025–26, with an overall write-off ratio of 33.2%.

Foreign Banks recorded a write-off ratio of 39.6% during FY2025–26.

Private Sector Banks relied more on loan write-offs and provisioning buffers to improve their balance sheets due to higher defaults in unsecured retail loans, microfinance, personal loans, credit cards, and unsecured business loans.

Public Sector Banks (PSBs) focused primarily on the long-term recovery of stressed assets instead of aggressive write-offs, despite holding the highest share of NPAs.

The write-off and recovery measures significantly improved the banking sector's asset quality, reducing the Gross Non- Performing Assets (GNPA) ratio to a multi- decade low of 1.8% in March 2026, compared to 7.3% in March 2021.

During the period FY2020–21 to FY2024– 25, Public Sector Banks wrote off approximately ₹5.81 lakh crore of bad loans, while Private Sector Banks wrote off around ₹3.09 lakh crore.

question: Recently, the White Rabbit Technology- based Indian Standard Time (IST) Distribution Demonstration Network was launched under which initiative?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The initiative has been launched under the vision of “One Nation, One Time” to establish a uniform, highly precise, secure, and indigenous Indian Standard Time (IST) network, reducing India’s dependence on foreign GPS-based time sources and strengthening digital sovereignty.

Detailed Explanation:

Union Minister Pralhad Joshi (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution (MoCAF&PD) and Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)) inaugurated the White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time (IST) Distribution Demonstration Network at the Regional Reference Standards Laboratory (RRSL), Jakkur, Bengaluru, Karnataka.

The initiative has been launched under the vision of “One Nation, One Time” to establish a uniform, highly precise, secure, and indigenous Indian Standard Time (IST) network, reducing India’s dependence on foreign GPS-based time sources and strengthening digital sovereignty.

The Demonstration Network enables the secure dissemination of UTC (NPLI)-traceable Indian Standard Time (IST) using Precision Time Protocol (PTP)-based White Rabbit Technology.

White Rabbit Technology is an Ethernet-based precision time synchronisation protocol that combines Precision Time Protocol (PTP) with Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE) to provide sub-nanosecond accuracy over fibre- optic networks.

The indigenous IST distribution system provides highly accurate, secure, resilient, and reliable time synchronisation for critical national infrastructure.

CSIR–Indian Institute of Chemical Technology (CSIR-IICT), Hyderabad has developed India's first indigenous process technology for manufacturing Hydrofluoroolefin-1234yf (HFO- 1234yf), a next-generation green refrigerant for refrigeration and air-conditioning systems.

HFO-1234yf is designed to replace Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) because it has Zero Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), Very Low Global Warming Potential (GWP), and a short atmospheric lifetime of about 11 days.

Detailed Explanation:

CSIR–Indian Institute of Chemical Technology (CSIR-IICT), Hyderabad has developed India's first indigenous process technology for manufacturing Hydrofluoroolefin-1234yf (HFO- 1234yf), a next-generation green refrigerant for refrigeration and air-conditioning systems.

HFO-1234yf is designed to replace Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) because it has Zero Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP), Very Low Global Warming Potential (GWP), and a short atmospheric lifetime of about 11 days.

In comparison, Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) have an atmospheric lifetime of around 13.8 years, making HFO-1234yf a more environmentally sustainable refrigerant.

The development supports India's commitment under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, which aims to phase down the production and consumption of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

India will implement the HFC phase- down in four stages, with 10% reduction in 2032, 20% in 2037, 30% in 2042, and 85% in 2047.

question: Recently, India's drug regulator (CDSCO) approved Novo Nordisk's Wegovy (Semaglutide Injection 2.4 mg) for the treatment of which disease?

question: Recently, India approved its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, developed by which company?
explanation:

India has approved its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, after receiving marketing authorisation from the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI), marking a major milestone in the country's fight against dengue.

QDENGA, developed by Takeda Biopharmaceuticals (Japan), is a live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine that provides protection against all four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4).

The vaccine is approved for individuals aged 4 to 60 years, irrespective of whether they have had a previous dengue infection.

Detailed Explanation:

India has approved its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, after receiving marketing authorisation from the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI), marking a major milestone in the country's fight against dengue.

QDENGA, developed by Takeda Biopharmaceuticals (Japan), is a live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine that provides protection against all four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4).

The vaccine is approved for individuals aged 4 to 60 years, irrespective of whether they have had a previous dengue infection.

QDENGA is administered in a two-dose schedule and does not require pre- vaccination screening, making it easier to include in immunisation programmes.

In the global TIDES Phase III Trial, the vaccine demonstrated 80.2% efficacy against laboratory-confirmed dengue one year after the second dose and 90.4% efficacy in preventing dengue-related hospitalisation 18 months after the second dose.

The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), granted marketing authorisation for Qdenga®, making it India's first approved dengue vaccine.

question: As per the news, the "Roadmap for Building India as a Leading Bioeconomy Powerhouse by 2035" aims to expand India's bioeconomy to what value by 2035?

explanation:
Short Explanation:

With the discovery of Beta Pictoris d, the Beta Pictoris system has become only the second known planetary system with at least three directly imaged planets.

Detailed Explanation:

Astronomers using National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) discovered a new giant exoplanet, Beta Pictoris d, located 63 light-years from Earth and estimated to be about 23 million years old.

With the discovery of Beta Pictoris d, the Beta Pictoris system has become only the second known planetary system with at least three directly imaged planets.

Beta Pictoris d orbits the nearby star Beta Pictoris, which already hosts Beta Pictoris b and Beta Pictoris c.

Beta Pictoris b is notable as one of the first exoplanets ever directly imaged, making the Beta Pictoris system historically significant in exoplanet research.

JWST’s Near-Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) detected the unique chemical fingerprint of Beta Pictoris d’s atmosphere, enabling its discovery.

Beta Pictoris d is estimated to have at least twice the mass of Jupiter, making it the smallest of the three known giant planets in the Beta Pictoris system.

Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

explanation:

Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) are exchange- traded securities introduced by the National Stock Exchange (NSE) that represent ownership of physical gold stored in SEBI- regulated vaults.

The NSE launched the Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR) Segment in May 2026 to provide a regulated, transparent and secure platform for buying and selling gold in electronic form.

Detailed Explanation:

Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) are exchange- traded securities introduced by the National Stock Exchange (NSE) that represent ownership of physical gold stored in SEBI- regulated vaults.

The NSE launched the Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR) Segment in May 2026 to provide a regulated, transparent and secure platform for buying and selling gold in electronic form.

question: As per the news, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has cautioned regulated entities against which cyber fraud that involves impersonation of senior company executives to trick employees into transferring funds?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has warned regulated entities and listed companies against the rising "Boss Scam", a cyber fraud primarily targeting finance and accounts departments.

In a Boss Scam, fraudsters impersonate Chief Executive Officers (CEOs), Managing Directors (MDs), or other senior executives to deceive employees into making unauthorised fund transfers.

SEBI issued the advisory after receiving inputs from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) regarding the increasing number of Boss Scam incidents.

Detailed Explanation:

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has warned regulated entities and listed companies against the rising "Boss Scam", a cyber fraud primarily targeting finance and accounts departments.

In a Boss Scam, fraudsters impersonate Chief Executive Officers (CEOs), Managing Directors (MDs), or other senior executives to deceive employees into making unauthorised fund transfers.

SEBI issued the advisory after receiving inputs from the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) regarding the increasing number of Boss Scam incidents.

Cybercriminals contact employees through emails, WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams, and social media platforms, pretending to be senior company officials and directing them to transfer funds to fraud-controlled bank accounts (mule accounts).

Fraudsters use Artificial Intelligence (AI)- based deepfake technology, including voice cloning, fake video calls, and fake social media groups, to create convincing identities of CEOs and senior executives.

In some cases, fraudsters falsely claim that the payment is related to Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI) and instruct employees to maintain strict secrecy, increasing the chances of successful fraud.

Since 2014, Indian Railways has electrified 48,072 route kilometres, compared to 21,801 route kilometres electrified during the previous six decades, making it one of the world's fastest railway electrification programmes.

All newly constructed railway lines and multi- tracking projects are now being developed with electrification from the initial stage.

Railway electrification has significantly reduced dependence on diesel. Diesel consumption declined from 293 crore litres (2015–16) to 108 crore litres (2024–25), saving fuel costs, reducing crude oil imports, and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

question: As per the news, scientists from the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology (IASST), Guwahati, demonstrated the first-ever use of Borophene as a high-performance lubricant additive in which oil?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

Scientists from the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology (IASST), Guwahati, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), achieved a major breakthrough by demonstrating the first-ever use of Borophene (2D nanomaterial) as a high- performance lubricant additive in castor oil.

The research is considered a significant advancement in sustainable lubrication technology and has the potential to transform renewable energy systems, marine applications, green lubrication technologies, and sustainable manufacturing.

Friction and wear are major causes of energy loss and equipment failure in industries, making the development of advanced lubricants an important scientific and technological objective.

Castor oil is a renewable, biodegradable, and environment-friendly lubricant, whose performance can be significantly enhanced using Borophene as an additive.

Detailed Explanation:

Scientists from the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology (IASST), Guwahati, an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), achieved a major breakthrough by demonstrating the first-ever use of Borophene (2D nanomaterial) as a high- performance lubricant additive in castor oil.

The research is considered a significant advancement in sustainable lubrication technology and has the potential to transform renewable energy systems, marine applications, green lubrication technologies, and sustainable manufacturing.

Friction and wear are major causes of energy loss and equipment failure in industries, making the development of advanced lubricants an important scientific and technological objective.

Castor oil is a renewable, biodegradable, and environment-friendly lubricant, whose performance can be significantly enhanced using Borophene as an additive.

The researchers found that adding only 0.1 wt.% Borophene to castor oil reduced friction by approximately 42% compared to pure castor oil.

The research was conducted under the guidance of Prof. Devasish Chowdhury, with Mr. Ujjibit Boruah, INSPIRE Senior Research Fellow (SRF), serving as the first author of the study.

Borophene dispersed uniformly in castor oil without requiring any chemical modification, making it suitable for practical lubricant applications.

question: As per the news, the Reserve Bank of India's Commercial Banks–Governance Amendment Directions, 2026 will come into effect from which date?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued the Commercial Banks–Governance Amendment Directions, 2026, which will come into effect from 1 October 2026.

The Amendment Directions aim to strengthen board governance, improve decision-making, and enhance corporate governance in the Indian banking sector.

The revised framework shifts from a prescriptive, theme-based approach to a principle-based governance framework, providing greater flexibility to bank boards.

Under the new framework, Boards of Directors will devote more attention to business strategy, risk management, financial resilience, and corporate governance.

Detailed Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued the Commercial Banks–Governance Amendment Directions, 2026, which will come into effect from 1 October 2026.

The Amendment Directions aim to strengthen board governance, improve decision-making, and enhance corporate governance in the Indian banking sector.

The revised framework shifts from a prescriptive, theme-based approach to a principle-based governance framework, providing greater flexibility to bank boards.

Under the new framework, Boards of Directors will devote more attention to business strategy, risk management, financial resilience, and corporate governance.

The Board will primarily oversee business strategy, risk management, governance standards, regulatory compliance, internal controls, and exposures to related entities.

Routine operational matters may be delegated to Board Committees or Management Committees, enabling the Board to focus on strategic oversight.

The Chairperson of the Board has been assigned the primary responsibility for setting the Board agenda, while the management must provide timely and adequate information for informed decision- making.

The Amendment Directions apply to Commercial Banks and, with suitable modifications, also to Private Sector Banks, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Payments Banks, and Local Area Banks (LABs).

The United Nations (UN) Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) released the State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) 2026 report titled “Understanding and Addressing the High Cost of a Healthy Diet.” The report estimated that 645 million people (7.8% of the global population) faced hunger in 2025, showing a slight improvement from 8.1% in the previous year.

Despite this progress, the world remains off track to achieve Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)-2: Zero Hunger by 2030.

Detailed Explanation:

The United Nations (UN) Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) released the State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) 2026 report titled “Understanding and Addressing the High Cost of a Healthy Diet.” The report estimated that 645 million people (7.8% of the global population) faced hunger in 2025, showing a slight improvement from 8.1% in the previous year.

Despite this progress, the world remains off track to achieve Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)-2: Zero Hunger by 2030.

The SOFI Report is jointly prepared by five UN specialized agencies:

Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) World Food Programme (WFP) World Health Organization (WHO) The number of hungry people in 2025 remained 61 million higher than pre- COVID-19 (2019) levels.

The global prevalence of hunger declined to 7.8% in 2025, compared to 8.0% in 2015, when the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development was adopted.

Under a quick-recovery scenario, the report projects the number of chronically undernourished people to decline to about 511 million by 2030.

If disruptions in oil, gas, and fertilizer supplies continue, the number of chronically undernourished people could remain as high as 522 million by 2030.

question: As per the news, India strengthened its Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with Sri Lanka by incorporating which internationally recognised anti-abuse provision?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

India has strengthened its Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with Sri Lanka by incorporating the Principal Purpose Test (PPT), an internationally recognised anti- abuse provision under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework.

The amendment was introduced through a Protocol notified by the Ministry of Finance and came into force on 19 June 2026 after completion of domestic legal procedures by both countries.

The revised provisions will apply in India for income derived from 1 April 2027.

Detailed Explanation:

India has strengthened its Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) with Sri Lanka by incorporating the Principal Purpose Test (PPT), an internationally recognised anti- abuse provision under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) framework.

The amendment was introduced through a Protocol notified by the Ministry of Finance and came into force on 19 June 2026 after completion of domestic legal procedures by both countries.

The revised provisions will apply in India for income derived from 1 April 2027.

The Principal Purpose Test (PPT) allows tax authorities of both countries to deny treaty benefits if one of the main purposes of a transaction or investment is found to be obtaining an undue tax advantage rather than carrying out genuine commercial activities.

The amendment aims to:

Prevent treaty shopping arrangements.

Avoid double non-taxation.

Ensure fair taxation while continuing to eliminate double taxation for genuine taxpayers.

The amendment does not change the existing tax rates under the India–Sri Lanka DTAA.

options.text: Import of foreign goods into India
Export of goods manufactured or produced in India

explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) relaxed the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Policy by allowing foreign-funded e-commerce companies to operate an inventory-based model exclusively for the export of goods manufactured or produced in Indi(a) The policy amendment is intended to strengthen India's manufacturing ecosystem, expand the country's global export footprint, and improve the competitiveness of Indian manufacturers in international markets.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoC&I) relaxed the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Policy by allowing foreign-funded e-commerce companies to operate an inventory-based model exclusively for the export of goods manufactured or produced in Indi(a) The policy change aims to boost India's exports by enabling foreign-invested e- commerce platforms to procure, stock, warehouse, and export Indian-made products directly to overseas consumers, thereby improving global market access for domestic manufacturers and sellers.

Under the previous FDI policy, foreign investment was permitted only in Business-to- Business (B2B) e-commerce and the marketplace model, while Business-to- Consumer (B2C) e-commerce and the inventory-based model were prohibited for foreign-funded entities to protect domestic retailers.

Under the revised FDI policy, the restrictions on the inventory-based model and B2C e- commerce will not apply when the goods being sold are manufactured or produced in India and are exported to foreign markets.

The updated policy permits foreign-funded e- commerce entities to own inventory, purchase, warehouse, and directly export domestically manufactured products to customers outside Indi(a) The policy amendment is intended to strengthen India's manufacturing ecosystem, expand the country's global export footprint, and improve the competitiveness of Indian manufacturers in international markets.

Scientists from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) discovered and documented two new spider species—Simonia lawbah from Meghalaya and Hamataliwa papikonda from Andhra Pradesh (AP)— highlighting India's rich and underexplored biodiversity.

The discoveries were published in the peer- reviewed journals Zootaxa and Records of the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), marking significant additions to India's arachnological records.

Simonia lawbah is the first recorded species of the genus Simonia in India, making it an important discovery for the country's biodiversity records.

Simonia lawbah constructs a distinctive cone- shaped ray web to capture flying insects.

Basel III-compliant AT-1 Perpetual Bonds are capital instruments that help banks strengthen their capital base, improve the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), and comply with Basel III regulatory norms.

Perpetual Bonds have no fixed maturity date, but they may include a call option, enabling the issuer to redeem them after a specified period.
