question: As per the news, the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath became India's which UNESCO World Heritage Site after its inscription during the 48th Session of the World Heritage Committee?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh (UP) was inscribed on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage List during the 48th Session of the World Heritage Committee (WHC) held in Busan, South Korea.

With this inscription, Sarnath became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site (WHS) and the 4th UNESCO World Heritage Site in Uttar Pradesh, after the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.

Detailed Explanation:

The Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh (UP) was inscribed on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage List during the 48th Session of the World Heritage Committee (WHC) held in Busan, South Korea.

With this inscription, Sarnath became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site (WHS) and the 4th UNESCO World Heritage Site in Uttar Pradesh, after the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.

Sarnath was included in UNESCO's Tentative List in 1998, and India submitted its nomination dossier in January 2025 for the 2025–26 World Heritage cycle.

The inscription recognizes the Outstanding Universal Value (OUV) of Sarnath as one of the world's holiest Buddhist pilgrimage centres, where Gautama Buddha (Lord Buddha) delivered his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta/Dharmachakra Pravartana) after attaining enlightenment.

Sarnath marks the beginning of the spread of Buddhist teachings and remains one of the most important Buddhist pilgrimage sites in the world.

India first proposed polymer banknotes in 2012

explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Government of India (GoI) has approved the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) proposal to conduct field trials of 1 billion (100 crore) polymer banknotes each in the ₹10 and ₹20 denominations, marking a major step towards introducing more durable and secure currency notes in India.

The proposal was submitted by the RBI, with the recommendation of its Central Board, under Section 25 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, seeking approval for field trials and the regular issuance of ₹10 and ₹20 polymer banknotes after successful completion of the trials.

question: As per the news, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed that all Securitisation Notes (SNs) must be issued, held, and transferred in which form?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released draft amendments proposing that all Securitisation Notes (SNs) must be issued, held, and transferred only in dematerialised (demat) form to enhance transparency, efficiency, liquidity, and investor protection in the securitisation market.

Securitisation Notes (SNs) are financial instruments created by pooling assets such as home loans, vehicle loans, and other retail loans, which are then sold to investors, enabling banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to raise fresh funds for further lending.

The RBI has proposed to retain the minimum investment size of ₹1 crore, which will apply both at the time of issuance and for every subsequent transfer of Securitisation Notes.

Detailed Explanation:

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released draft amendments proposing that all Securitisation Notes (SNs) must be issued, held, and transferred only in dematerialised (demat) form to enhance transparency, efficiency, liquidity, and investor protection in the securitisation market.

Securitisation Notes (SNs) are financial instruments created by pooling assets such as home loans, vehicle loans, and other retail loans, which are then sold to investors, enabling banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to raise fresh funds for further lending.

The RBI has proposed to retain the minimum investment size of ₹1 crore, which will apply both at the time of issuance and for every subsequent transfer of Securitisation Notes.

The draft framework requires agreements between lenders and Special Purpose Entities (SPEs) to ensure continuous compliance with the ₹1 crore minimum investment requirement throughout the life cycle of the securities.

According to the proposal, an issue of Securitisation Notes (SNs) will be treated as a public issue if it is offered to the number of investors specified under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulations.

The proposed amendments aim to strengthen the regulatory framework for securitisation, improve market transparency, facilitate efficient trading, and enhance the overall functioning of India's debt and securitisation market.

The RBI has invited public comments and stakeholder feedback on the draft proposals until 27 August 2026.

question: As per the news, which index will replace the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) as the GDP deflator for quarterly and annual GDP estimates, wherever applicable?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) announced that the Output Producer Price Index (PPI) will replace the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) as the GDP deflator for quarterly and annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates, wherever applicable.

The Producer Price Index (PPI) series was released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in June 2026 to improve GDP measurement and align India's National Accounts with international statistical standards.

Detailed Explanation:

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) announced that the Output Producer Price Index (PPI) will replace the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) as the GDP deflator for quarterly and annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates, wherever applicable.

The Producer Price Index (PPI) series was released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in June 2026 to improve GDP measurement and align India's National Accounts with international statistical standards.

The Output PPI will be used for GDP deflation, improving the accuracy of real GDP growth estimates by reducing distortions caused by the earlier methodology.

Under the revised GDP series, the base year has been updated from 2011–12 to 2022–23, reflecting the latest economic structure and production patterns.

The revised methodology adopts the Double Deflation approach, which separately adjusts output prices and input prices, providing a more accurate measure of real value added.

The earlier Single Deflation method, which used the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for both output and input prices, is being replaced due to its tendency to distort GDP growth estimates.

question: As per the news, what is the name of NASA's proposed AI-powered mission concept for the first-ever direct collection and in-situ analysis of particles from Saturn's rings?
explanation:
Short Explanation:

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has proposed an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered mission concept named PRAXIS (Planetary Rings Autonomous EXploration with In-situ Sampling) under Phase I of the NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) 2026 Program.

The PRAXIS mission aims to achieve the first- ever direct collection and in-situ analysis of particles from Saturn's rings, addressing one of the highest priorities in planetary science decadal surveys.

Detailed Explanation:

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has proposed an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered mission concept named PRAXIS (Planetary Rings Autonomous EXploration with In-situ Sampling) under Phase I of the NASA Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) 2026 Program.

The PRAXIS mission aims to achieve the first- ever direct collection and in-situ analysis of particles from Saturn's rings, addressing one of the highest priorities in planetary science decadal surveys.

The project is being led by Dr. B. Marco Quadrelli, Principal and Group Supervisor of the Robotics Modelling and Simulation Group at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in California, United States (USA).

The primary objective of PRAXIS is to provide the first direct observations of millimetre- to centimetre-sized (mm–cm) ring particles, which were not directly studied by NASA's Cassini mission.

Saturn's rings are composed mainly of water ice and contain particles ranging from tiny grains to house-sized boulders, which continuously collide, merge, and break apart.

The mission will use an AI-powered, bio- inspired robotic explorer equipped with robotic autonomy, collision avoidance, precision sampling, and real-time in-situ scientific analysis to safely collect and study ring particles.

question: As per the news, what is the name of the newly discovered polypore (bracket) fungus species found in Kolhapur, Maharashtra?

question: As per the news, which of the following statements about the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 is correct?

options.text: The maximum fine for organised examination- related crimes has been increased to ₹10 crore
The maximum imprisonment for organised examination-related crimes has been reduced to 5 years.
The debarment period for service providers has been reduced from 4 years to 2 years
The maximum fine for individuals using unfair means remains ₹10 lakh
The Bill does not provide for Special Fast Track Courts

explanation:
The Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by a voice vote to strengthen the legal framework against the use of unfair means in public examinations and protect the interests of students and job aspirants.

Punishment for individuals using unfair means has been increased from 3–5 years to 5–10 years imprisonment, with the maximum fine raised from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh.

For service providers involved in examination malpractices, the maximum fine has been increased from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore, and the debarment period from conducting public examinations has been extended from 4 years to 8 years.

Punishment for directors and senior management of service providers has been enhanced to 5–10 years' imprisonment, along with a maximum fine of ₹5 crore.

Punishment for organised examination-related crimes has been increased from 5–10 years to 7–10 years' imprisonment, while the maximum fine has been enhanced from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore.

The Bill also provides for the establishment of Special Fast Track Courts for offences related to public examinations, with investigations to be completed within 2 months and trials within 3 months from the filing of the charge sheet.
